JDG.1.1-3.text: Judah and Simeon agree to fight the Canaanites together

JDG.1.4-5.text: The LORD helps Judah defeat the Canaanites at Bezek

JDG.1.6-7.text: Judah captures Adoni-bezek, who dies in Jerusalem

JDG.1.8-10.text: Judah captures Jerusalem and fights at Hebron

JDG.1.11-13.text: Othniel captures Debir and marries Caleb’s daughter Acsah

JDG.1.14-15.text: Acsah asks her father Caleb for springs of water

JDG.1.16-17.text: Kenites join Judah; Judah and Simeon destroy Zephath

JDG.1.18-19.text: Judah takes the hill country but not the plains

JDG.1.20-21.text: Caleb gets Hebron; Benjamites cannot drive out Jebusites

JDG.1.22-24.text: The house of Joseph attacks Bethel and sends spies

JDG.1.25-26.text: Joseph’s men destroy Bethel but free the helpful man

JDG.1.27-28.text: Manasseh fails to drive out the Canaanites

JDG.1.29-29.text: Ephraim fails to drive out the Canaanites in Gezer

JDG.1.30-30.text: Zebulun fails to drive out the people of Kitron and Nahalol

JDG.1.31-32.text: Asher fails to drive out the people of seven towns

JDG.1.33-33.text: Naphtali lives among the Canaanites of Beth-shemesh

JDG.1.34-36.text: The Amorites push the Danites into the hill country

JDG.2.1-2.text: The angel of the LORD says Israel has not obeyed

JDG.2.3-5.text: The LORD will not drive out the nations; Israel weeps

JDG.2.6-8.text: Israel serves the LORD during Joshua’s life; Joshua dies

JDG.2.10-10.text: A new generation rises that does not know the LORD

JDG.2.11-13.text: Israel leaves the LORD and serves Baal and Ashtoreths

JDG.2.14-15.text: The LORD is angry and lets enemies overpower Israel

JDG.2.16-17.text: The LORD raises up judges, but Israel does not listen

JDG.2.18-19.text: Israel turns back to evil when each judge dies

JDG.2.20-23.text: The LORD will leave the nations to test Israel

JDG.3.1-3.text: The nations left in Canaan to teach Israel war

check.why: The title is a noun phrase rather than a full sentence statement.
check.suggestion: The LORD leaves nations in Canaan to teach Israel war

JDG.3.4-6.text: Israel marries people of the land and serves other gods

JDG.3.7-8.text: Israel forgets the LORD and serves King Cushan-rishathaim

JDG.3.9-11.text: The LORD raises up Othniel to save Israel

JDG.3.12-14.text: Eglon king of Moab rules Israel for eighteen years

JDG.3.15-15.text: The LORD raises up Ehud, who brings tribute to Eglon

JDG.3.16-18.text: Ehud makes a sword and brings tribute to Eglon

JDG.3.19-20.text: Ehud tells King Eglon he has a secret message

JDG.3.21-23.text: Ehud kills King Eglon and locks the doors

JDG.3.24-25.text: Eglon’s servants find the king dead

JDG.3.26-27.text: Ehud escapes and blows the ram’s horn in Ephraim

JDG.3.28-30.text: Israel defeats Moab and has rest for eighty years

JDG.4.1-3.text: Jabin of Canaan oppresses the Israelites for twenty years

JDG.4.6-7.text: Deborah tells Barak to lead ten thousand men to Tabor

JDG.4.8-9.text: Barak will go only if Deborah goes with him

JDG.4.10-10.text: Barak calls men from Zebulun and Naphtali

JDG.4.11-11.text: Heber the Kenite pitches his tent near Kedesh

JDG.4.12-13.text: Sisera hears about Barak and gathers his chariots

JDG.4.14-14.text: Barak goes down from Mount Tabor to fight Sisera

JDG.4.15-16.text: The LORD defeats Sisera’s army before Barak

JDG.4.17-18.text: Sisera flees to Jael’s tent and Jael welcomes him

JDG.4.19-20.text: Sisera asks Jael for water and to watch the entrance

JDG.4.21-22.text: Jael kills Sisera with a tent peg

check.why: The draft only describes verse 21 and leaves out Barak finding Sisera dead in verse 22.
check.suggestion: Jael kills Sisera and shows him dead to Barak

JDG.4.23-24.text: God subdues Jabin before the Israelites

JDG.5.1-2.text: Deborah and Barak begin to sing to the LORD

JDG.5.3-4.text: Deborah sings praise to the LORD, God of Israel

JDG.5.5-6.text: The mountains shake before the LORD; roads are empty

JDG.5.7-8.text: Deborah arises when Israel chooses new gods

check.why: The text says war came when Israel chose new gods, not that Deborah arose then.
check.suggestion: Deborah arises after war comes to Israel

JDG.5.9-10.text: Deborah praises the volunteers and blesses the LORD

JDG.5.11-11.text: The singers tell of the LORD’s righteous acts

JDG.5.12-13.text: Deborah and Barak are called to arise and sing

JDG.5.14-14.text: Tribes of Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir and Zebulun join

JDG.5.15-15.text: Issachar joins Barak, but Reuben cannot decide

JDG.5.16-16.text: Reuben stays with the sheep and does not help

JDG.5.17-18.text: Some tribes stay away, but Zebulun and Naphtali fight

JDG.5.19-20.text: The kings of Canaan fight, and the stars fight Sisera

JDG.5.21-22.text: The River Kishon sweeps away Sisera’s army

JDG.5.23-23.text: The angel of the LORD curses Meroz for not helping

JDG.5.24-25.text: Deborah blesses Jael for giving Sisera milk and curds

check.why: The text does not say Jael is blessed for giving Sisera milk and curds.
check.suggestion: Jael is blessed and gives Sisera milk and curds

JDG.5.26-27.text: Jael strikes Sisera and he falls dead at her feet

JDG.5.28-28.text: Sisera’s mother wonders why his chariot is late

JDG.5.29-30.text: Sisera’s mother tells herself the army is taking spoil

JDG.5.31-31.text: The song ends and the land rests for forty years

JDG.6.1-2.text: Israel does evil and hides from Midian in the mountains

JDG.6.3-4.text: Midian and others destroy Israel’s crops and animals

JDG.6.5-6.text: Midian comes like locusts and Israel cries to the LORD

JDG.6.7-8.text: God sends a prophet who reminds Israel of Egypt

JDG.6.9-10.text: The prophet says Israel did not obey the LORD

JDG.6.11-12.text: The LORD’s angel greets Gideon as a mighty man

JDG.6.13-13.text: Gideon asks why the LORD has forsaken Israel

JDG.6.14-15.text: The LORD tells Gideon to save Israel from Midian

JDG.6.16-18.text: The LORD promises to be with Gideon who asks for a sign

JDG.6.19-20.text: Gideon prepares a meal and puts it on the rock

JDG.6.21-21.text: Fire burns Gideon’s offering and the angel vanishes

JDG.6.22-24.text: Gideon fears he will die, but the LORD gives him peace

JDG.6.25-26.text: The LORD tells Gideon to destroy Baal’s altar

JDG.6.27-27.text: Gideon destroys the altar at night because he is afraid

JDG.6.28-29.text: The city men learn that Gideon tore down the altar

JDG.6.30-30.text: The city men tell Joash to bring out Gideon to die

JDG.6.31-32.text: Joash defends Gideon and Gideon gets the name Jerubbaal

JDG.6.33-33.text: Midian and other armies camp in the Valley of Jezreel

JDG.6.34-35.text: The Spirit of the LORD comes on Gideon, who gathers men

JDG.6.36-37.text: Gideon asks God for a sign with a wool fleece

JDG.6.38-38.text: God makes dew fall only on the fleece

JDG.6.39-40.text: Gideon asks for a second sign, and the fleece stays dry

JDG.7.1-1.text: Gideon’s army camps at the spring of Harod

JDG.7.2-3.text: The LORD says the army is too big, and many go home

JDG.7.4-4.text: The LORD tells Gideon to bring the men to the water

JDG.7.5-6.text: The LORD chooses three hundred men who lap water

JDG.7.7-8.text: Gideon keeps three hundred men and sends the rest home

JDG.7.9-11.text: The LORD sends Gideon to listen at Midian’s camp

JDG.7.12-12.text: Midian’s army is as many as locusts and sand

JDG.7.13-14.text: A Midianite’s dream shows that Gideon will win

JDG.7.15-16.text: Gideon worships and divides the men into three companies

JDG.7.17-18.text: Gideon tells his men to blow horns and shout

JDG.7.19-19.text: Gideon and his 100 men blow horns and break jars

JDG.7.20-21.text: The Midianite army runs away as Gideon’s men shout

JDG.7.22-23.text: The LORD turns the Midianites against each other

JDG.7.24-25.text: Ephraim captures Oreb and Zeeb, princes of Midian

JDG.8.1-1.text: The men of Ephraim angrily accuse Gideon

JDG.8.2-3.text: Gideon calms Ephraim with a kind answer

JDG.8.4-5.text: Gideon asks the men of Succoth for bread

JDG.8.6-7.text: Succoth refuses bread and Gideon threatens punishment

JDG.8.8-9.text: Penuel refuses Gideon, who threatens its tower

JDG.8.10-10.text: Zebah and Zalmunna wait in Karkor with 15,000 men

check.why: The text states that Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, not that they were waiting.
check.suggestion: Zebah and Zalmunna are in Karkor with 15,000 men

JDG.8.11-12.text: Gideon defeats the army and captures Midian’s kings

JDG.8.13-14.text: A young man writes the names of Succoth’s leaders

JDG.8.15-17.text: Gideon punishes the men of Succoth and Penuel

JDG.8.18-19.text: Gideon learns the men killed at Tabor were his brothers

JDG.8.20-21.text: Gideon kills Zebah and Zalmunna himself

JDG.8.22-23.text: Gideon refuses to rule Israel; the LORD will rule

JDG.8.24-25.text: Gideon asks the Israelites for gold earrings

JDG.8.26-26.text: The gold Gideon gathered weighs 1,700 shekels

JDG.8.27-27.text: Gideon makes an ephod, and Israel worships it

JDG.8.28-28.text: Midian is subdued and does not rise again

JDG.8.29-31.text: Gideon has seventy sons and a son named Abimelech

JDG.8.32-33.text: Gideon dies, and Israel turns to worship Baal

JDG.8.34-35.text: Israel forgets the LORD and is unkind to Gideon’s family

JDG.9.1-2.text: Abimelech asks the Shechem leaders to make him ruler

check.why: Abimelech asks his mother’s clan to speak to the leaders, rather than asking the leaders directly.
check.suggestion: Abimelech asks his relatives to speak to Shechem’s leaders

JDG.9.3-4.text: Shechem’s leaders give Abimelech silver to hire men

JDG.9.5-6.text: Abimelech kills his brothers and Shechem makes him king

JDG.9.7-8.text: Jotham tells how the trees wanted a king

JDG.9.9-11.text: The olive tree and the fig tree refuse to be king

JDG.9.12-14.text: The grapevine refuses, and the thornbush is asked

JDG.9.15-16.text: The thornbush warns of fire; Jotham questions Shechem

JDG.9.17-18.text: Jotham says Shechem wronged his father’s family

JDG.9.19-21.text: Jotham warns of fire and runs away to Beer

JDG.9.22-24.text: God turns Shechem’s leaders against Abimelech

JDG.9.25-25.text: Shechem’s leaders set an ambush against Abimelech

JDG.9.26-27.text: Gaal comes to Shechem and its leaders curse Abimelech

JDG.9.28-29.text: Gaal says the Shechemites should not serve Abimelech

JDG.9.30-31.text: Zebul angrily sends a secret message to Abimelech

JDG.9.32-33.text: Zebul tells Abimelech to hide and attack at sunrise

JDG.9.34-35.text: Abimelech’s troops hide near Shechem in four companies

JDG.9.36-37.text: Gaal sees people coming; Zebul says it is only shadows

JDG.9.38-40.text: Zebul mocks Gaal, and Gaal fights Abimelech and flees

JDG.9.41-43.text: Zebul drives Gaal out, and Abimelech attacks the people

JDG.9.44-45.text: Abimelech captures Shechem, destroys it and sows salt

JDG.9.46-47.text: Shechem’s leaders gather in the temple of El-berith

JDG.9.48-49.text: Abimelech burns the tower and kills about a thousand people

JDG.9.50-51.text: Abimelech captures Thebez, but the people flee to a tower

JDG.9.52-54.text: A woman drops a millstone on Abimelech, and he dies

JDG.9.55-57.text: God repays the wickedness of Abimelech and Shechem

JDG.10.6-7.text: The Israelites serve other gods and the LORD is angry

JDG.10.8-9.text: Ammonites and Philistines oppress Israel for 18 years

JDG.10.10-12.text: The Israelites cry out to the LORD and confess sin

check.why: The draft covers only verse 10 and leaves out the LORD’s reply in verses 11–12.
check.suggestion: The Israelites confess sin, and the LORD replies

JDG.10.13-14.text: The LORD says he will no longer save Israel

JDG.10.15-16.text: Israel puts away foreign gods and serves the LORD

JDG.10.17-18.text: Gilead’s rulers look for a leader against the Ammonites

JDG.11.1-3.text: Jephthah’s brothers send him away, and he lives in Tob

JDG.11.4-6.text: The elders of Gilead ask Jephthah to command the army

JDG.11.7-8.text: Jephthah questions the elders, who ask him to lead Gilead

JDG.11.9-11.text: Jephthah becomes Gilead’s leader and states his terms

JDG.11.12-13.text: Jephthah asks the Ammonite king why he attacks Israel

check.why: The draft covers only Jephthah’s question in verse 12 and omits the Ammonite king’s response in verse 13.
check.suggestion: Jephthah questions the Ammonite king, who demands his land

JDG.11.14-16.text: Jephthah tells the Ammonite king about Israel’s journey

JDG.11.17-18.text: Edom and Moab refuse Israel passage, so Israel goes around

JDG.11.19-20.text: Sihon refuses Israel passage and fights Israel

JDG.11.21-22.text: The LORD helps Israel defeat Sihon and take the land

JDG.11.23-25.text: Jephthah says the LORD gave Israel the land

JDG.11.26-28.text: Jephthah says Israel has held the land for 300 years

check.why: The draft covers only verse 26 and misses the Ammonite king’s refusal to listen in verse 28.
check.suggestion: Jephthah defends Israel, but the Ammonite king ignores him

JDG.11.29-31.text: Jephthah vows to give the LORD whatever greets him

JDG.11.32-33.text: The LORD helps Jephthah defeat the Ammonites

JDG.11.34-35.text: Jephthah sees his daughter and is filled with grief

JDG.11.36-37.text: Jephthah’s daughter asks for two months to mourn

JDG.11.38-40.text: Jephthah’s daughter returns, and Israel remembers her

JDG.12.1-2.text: The men of Ephraim threaten Jephthah

JDG.12.3-4.text: Jephthah answers Ephraim and fights against them

JDG.12.5-6.text: The Gileadites kill Ephraimites at the Jordan fords

JDG.12.7-7.text: Jephthah dies after judging Israel six years

JDG.12.10-12.text: Ibzan dies, and Elon judges Israel ten years

JDG.12.13-15.text: Abdon judges Israel eight years and then dies

JDG.13.1-2.text: Israel is under the Philistines, and Manoah has no child

JDG.13.3-5.text: The angel tells Manoah’s wife she will have a son

JDG.13.6-7.text: Manoah’s wife tells her husband what the man said

JDG.13.8-9.text: Manoah prays, and the angel comes to his wife again

JDG.13.10-11.text: Manoah’s wife brings her husband to the man

JDG.13.12-14.text: The angel tells Manoah that his wife must obey the rules

JDG.13.15-16.text: Manoah offers food, but the angel asks for an offering

check.why: The angel does not ask for an offering, but says that any burnt offering should be made to the LORD.
check.suggestion: Manoah offers food, but the angel refuses to eat

JDG.13.17-18.text: Manoah asks the angel’s name, but he will not tell it

JDG.13.19-20.text: Manoah makes an offering, and the angel rises in the flame

JDG.13.21-22.text: Manoah knows it was the angel and fears he will die

JDG.13.23-23.text: Manoah’s wife explains why God will not kill them

JDG.13.24-25.text: Samson is born and grows, and the Spirit stirs him

JDG.14.1-2.text: Samson asks his parents to get a Philistine wife for him

JDG.14.3-4.text: Samson’s parents object, but he insists on the woman

JDG.14.5-6.text: Samson kills a young lion with his bare hands

JDG.14.7-7.text: Samson goes down and speaks to the Philistine woman

JDG.14.8-9.text: Samson finds honey in the dead lion and eats it

JDG.14.10-11.text: Samson holds a feast, and thirty Philistine men join him

JDG.14.12-13.text: Samson offers the thirty men a riddle and a bet

JDG.14.14-14.text: Samson tells the riddle, and the men cannot solve it

JDG.14.15-15.text: The Philistines threaten Samson’s wife to learn the answer

JDG.14.16-17.text: Samson’s wife weeps until he tells her the answer

JDG.14.18-18.text: The men solve the riddle, and Samson answers angrily

JDG.14.19-20.text: Samson kills thirty men, and his wife is given away

JDG.15.1-2.text: Samson’s father-in-law will not let him see his wife

JDG.15.3-4.text: Samson ties torches to the tails of three hundred foxes

JDG.15.5-6.text: Samson burns Philistine fields; Philistines burn his wife

JDG.15.7-8.text: Samson takes revenge and kills many Philistines

JDG.15.9-10.text: The Philistines camp in Judah to arrest Samson

JDG.15.11-11.text: Men of Judah question Samson about his actions

JDG.15.12-13.text: Men of Judah tie up Samson to give him to the Philistines

JDG.15.14-14.text: God’s Spirit gives Samson power to break the ropes

JDG.15.15-16.text: Samson kills a thousand men with a donkey’s jawbone

JDG.15.17-18.text: Samson names the place and asks God for water

JDG.15.19-20.text: God gives Samson water, and Samson judges Israel

JDG.16.1-2.text: Samson goes to Gaza, and the Gazites wait to kill him

JDG.16.3-3.text: Samson carries the city gate to a mountain near Hebron

JDG.16.4-5.text: Philistine lords ask Delilah to find Samson’s secret

JDG.16.6-7.text: Samson lies to Delilah about seven fresh bowstrings

JDG.16.8-9.text: Samson breaks the bowstrings that Delilah tied

JDG.16.10-12.text: Samson breaks new ropes after lying to Delilah again

JDG.16.13-14.text: Samson lies about his hair, and pulls out the loom pin

JDG.16.15-16.text: Delilah presses Samson every day to tell his secret

JDG.16.17-17.text: Samson tells Delilah the secret of his strength

JDG.16.18-19.text: Delilah has Samson’s hair cut and his strength leaves

JDG.16.20-22.text: The Philistines capture Samson and blind him

JDG.16.23-24.text: The Philistines praise Dagon for Samson’s capture

JDG.16.25-26.text: Samson is brought out to entertain the Philistines

JDG.16.27-27.text: The temple is full of Philistines watching Samson

JDG.16.28-29.text: Samson prays to God for strength and grips the pillars

JDG.16.30-31.text: Samson pulls down the temple and dies with the Philistines

JDG.17.1-2.text: Micah returns the stolen silver to his mother

check.why: Micah confesses that he took the silver, but he does not return it until verse 3.
check.suggestion: Micah admits to his mother that he took her silver

JDG.17.3-4.text: Micah’s mother has silver idols made for his house

JDG.17.5-6.text: Micah sets up a shrine and makes his son a priest

JDG.17.7-9.text: A young Levite from Bethlehem comes to Micah’s house

JDG.17.10-11.text: Micah asks the Levite to be his priest and father

JDG.17.12-13.text: Micah ordains the Levite and expects God’s favor

JDG.18.1-2.text: The Danites send five men to look for land

JDG.18.3-4.text: The Danite spies question the young Levite

JDG.18.5-6.text: The priest tells the Danite men to go in peace

JDG.18.7-8.text: The spies see that the people of Laish feel safe

JDG.18.9-10.text: The spies urge the Danites to take the good land

JDG.18.11-12.text: Six hundred armed Danites camp near Kiriath-jearim

JDG.18.13-13.text: The Danites come to Micah’s house in Ephraim

JDG.18.14-14.text: The spies tell the Danites about Micah’s idols

JDG.18.15-16.text: The Danites greet the young Levite at Micah’s house

JDG.18.17-18.text: The spies take the idols, and the priest asks why

JDG.18.19-20.text: The Danites ask the Levite to be priest for a tribe

JDG.18.21-23.text: Micah and his neighbors chase the Danites

JDG.18.24-26.text: Micah complains, but the Danites threaten him and leave

JDG.18.27-29.text: The Danites burn Laish and build the city of Dan

JDG.18.30-31.text: The Danites set up idols with Jonathan as priest

JDG.19.1-2.text: A Levite’s concubine leaves him and goes to Bethlehem

JDG.19.3-4.text: The Levite stays three days with his father-in-law

JDG.19.5-6.text: The father-in-law urges the Levite to stay longer

JDG.19.7-8.text: The father-in-law again persuades the Levite to wait

JDG.19.9-9.text: The father-in-law asks the Levite to stay one more night

JDG.19.10-11.text: The Levite refuses to stay and travels toward Jebus

JDG.19.12-13.text: The Levite passes a foreign city and goes on to Gibeah

check.why: The Levite only says that they will go on to Gibeah, rather than actually traveling there in these verses.
check.suggestion: The Levite refuses to stay in a foreign city

JDG.19.14-15.text: No one in Gibeah takes the Levite in for the night

JDG.19.16-17.text: An old man in Gibeah asks the Levite where he is going

JDG.19.18-19.text: The Levite tells the old man that no one took him in

JDG.19.20-21.text: The old man takes the Levite into his house

JDG.19.22-23.text: Wicked men of Gibeah demand to abuse the Levite

JDG.19.24-26.text: The Levite sends his concubine out, and the men abuse her

JDG.19.27-28.text: The Levite finds his concubine collapsed at the door

JDG.19.29-30.text: The Levite sends pieces of his concubine through Israel

JDG.20.1-2.text: The Israelites gather at Mizpah before the LORD

JDG.20.3-4.text: The Israelites ask the Levite what happened

JDG.20.5-7.text: The Levite accuses the men of Gibeah and asks for advice

JDG.20.8-9.text: The Israelites all agree to go against Gibeah

JDG.20.10-11.text: Israel plans to supply the army and attack Gibeah

JDG.20.12-14.text: The Benjamites refuse to hand over the wicked men

JDG.20.15-16.text: Benjamin gathers 26,000 swordsmen and 700 skilled men

JDG.20.18-18.text: God tells the Israelites that Judah must go first

JDG.20.19-21.text: Benjamin defeats Israel and kills 22,000 men

JDG.20.22-23.text: God tells Israel to fight Benjamin again

JDG.20.26-26.text: The Israelites weep, fast, and offer offerings at Bethel

JDG.20.27-28.text: God says Israel will defeat Benjamin tomorrow

JDG.20.29-30.text: Israel sets an ambush around Gibeah

JDG.20.31-31.text: Benjamin chases Israel and kills about thirty men

JDG.20.32-33.text: Israel retreats to draw Benjamin away from the city

JDG.20.34-35.text: The LORD defeats Benjamin and Israel kills 25,100 men

JDG.20.36-38.text: The men in ambush attack the city of Gibeah

JDG.20.39-39.text: Benjamin thinks Israel is defeated again

JDG.20.40-41.text: Benjamin sees the city burning and is terrified

JDG.20.42-42.text: The Benjamites flee to the wilderness and are killed

JDG.20.43-44.text: Israel surrounds Benjamin and 18,000 Benjamites fall

JDG.20.45-46.text: Israel kills Benjamites as they flee toward Rimmon

JDG.20.47-48.text: Six hundred Benjamites escape and Israel burns the cities

JDG.21.1-3.text: Israel weeps because one tribe is missing

JDG.21.4-5.text: The Israelites build an altar and ask who stayed away

JDG.21.6-7.text: The Israelites grieve for Benjamin and ask about wives

JDG.21.8-10.text: Israel sends men to attack Jabesh-gilead

JDG.21.11-12.text: The men find 400 young women at Jabesh-gilead

JDG.21.13-15.text: The Benjamites receive the women but still need more

JDG.21.16-17.text: The elders ask how to get wives for the Benjamites

JDG.21.18-19.text: The elders remember the yearly feast at Shiloh

JDG.21.20-21.text: The Benjamites are told to catch wives at Shiloh

JDG.21.22-22.text: The elders will answer the men who complain

JDG.21.23-24.text: The Benjamites take wives and return home

JDG.21.25-25.text: Israel had no king, so everyone did what seemed right
